SBP: Strategize going forward: referral to psychiatry for psychotherapy and medication to improve coping
ICS: Assess the patient’s perception – Wilma: “It’s nothing, right?”

Giving knowledge to the patient. Learner should use lead-in narrative, then use “a part of” language: “I know that you are very positive and hopeful, yet I wonder if **a part of you** isn’t worried. I want to speak to that part.” Learner should give knowledge in small amounts while monitoring your reaction/emotion.

Address emotions (RAP), empathy. Learner should reflect your denial: “it’s very difficult for you to talk about this.” *If learner is empathic and understanding, you can break down and express your overarching fear of being overcome by the cancer and have uncontrollable pain. Learner should validate this as a very common concern.*
Sustain hope for control from second line chemotherapy – not cure, but something to hope for in addition to maintaining hope that her symptoms will be well controlled in your care.
Support coping – Brother very supportive, offers to have her move in with him for time being; recruit clergy from her church
Statement of support: Offer ongoing, personal support
